name: Astradhari
body:
Archetypes

Sangyarishi (Astradhari Archetype)
Soul Channeller (Astradhari Archetype)

Bearers of the weapons and armors of the gods, the astradhari are trained in ancient summoning techniques, letting them call idealized arms from powerful legendary beings, called astras, to their hands. They also develop a connection to the plane of memory for various purposes, like learning how to battle like the original wielders of astras or gaining obscure knowledge. Outside of their mystical abilities, the astradhari can fight as well as any warrior and develop a limited pool of essence.

Role: Astradhari are warriors, and as such their place is in the middle of combat. Depending on their astras, astradhari can fight at range, get toe-to-toe with their enemies, or protect their allies. They are also knowledgeable in many areas, and this knowledge can give them an edge over their enemies. In some lands they are known as warrior sages. Astradhari training is not impeded by one’s moral or ethical outlooks.

Alignment: Any.

Starting Wealth: 5d6 x 10 gp (average 175 gp). In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Hit Dice: d10

Class Skills

The astradhari’s class skills are: Appraise (Int), Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Heal (Wis), Knowledge (arcana) (Int), Knowledge (history) (Int), Knowledge (local) (Int), Knowledge (nobility) (Int), Knowledge (planes) (Int), Knowledge (religion) (Int), Ride (Dex), Swim (Str) and Use Magical Device (Cha).

Skill Ranks per Level: 4 + Int modifier.

Class Features

All of the following are class features of the astradhari:

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

Astradhari are proficient with all simple and martial weapons and with all armor (heavy, light, and medium), plus shields (but not with tower shields). The Astradhari are also automatically proficient with any astra they summon (see the astra summoning ability).

Essence (Su)

The astradhari’s training includes essence development. An astradhari has a pool of essence equal to half their class level (rounded down, minimum one).

Akashic Knowledge (Su)

At 1st level, an astradhari develops a connection with the Akashic Records, which powers most of their supernatural abilities. Each day, an astradhari can meditate and commune with the plane of memory for one hour, to change selected abilities. During this communion, an Astradhari sifts through certain records and can focus on a specific field, receiving an insight bonus equal to their essence capacity (gained by character and class levels), which can be divided amongst any Intelligence-based skills that they have ranks in. By taking a point of essence burn as a swift action, an astradhari can reassign this bonus. At 5th level, by applying at least a +2 bonus to a skill the astradhari can unlock it, as if they had the Signature Skill feat for that skill. At 10th level, an astradhari can apply this bonus to any skill they have ranks in.

Astra Summoning (Su)

At 1st level, an astradhari learns how to summon armors, shields and weapons from materialized legends and the patterns of the cosmos. While not veilweavers or starcallers in the normal sense, their training and knowledge of the akashic arts gives them abilities similar to these akashic practitioners. This enables them to summon these akashic emanations in the form of astras.

The astradhari uses Intelligence to determine their veilweaving and starcalling modifiers, and has a veilweaver and starcaller levels equal to their class level

The saving throw DCs of the astradhari’s veils are equal to 10 + the essence invested in the veil + their veilweaving modifier. The saving throw DCs for their constellations is 10+1/2 their starcaller level + their starcalling modifier unless stated otherwise. Unless they gain the ability to do so from another source, this does not grant them the ability to shape veils or manifest constellations normally. The veils they can shape and constellations they can manifest are determined by their ceremonial akashic arts ability.

Twice per day as a swift action, the astradhari can summon one astra from their list for 10 minutes. They can expend multiple uses of this ability as a part of the same swift action. If the astra summoned is a constellation, the astradhari still has to pay the essence burn cost to summon it. An astradhari can invest essence in the summoned astra as part of the summoning process. At 5th level and every 4 levels thereafter, an astradhari can use this ability one additional time per day. Additionally, they can take 2 points of essence drain to summon an astra without expending one of their daily uses of this ability (essence drain is like essence burn, except that it cannot be recovered and lasts until the character can rest for the day).

A summoned astra appears already shaped, in hand or worn; in the case of summoning an armor astra while already wearing an armor, the worn armor disappears for the duration of the summon. An astra cannot be given to another creature. If an astra is taken by another creature, or if it leaves the astradhari’s possession for any reason other than for being used as part of a ranged attack, it disappears and reappears in the astradhari’s possession at the beginning of their turn. Astradhari can summon any number of astras as part of the same action, as long as they can wield or wear them at the same time and have available uses of this ability to use or essence to drain.

If a summoned astra is destroyed, its duration ends. It can be summoned again by spending another use of summon astra or taking essence drain. If the astradhari enters an area of dead magic, an antimagic field, or a place where summoning spells are suppressed, the astra is suppressed while the astradhari remains in that area.

Ceremonial Akashic Arts

By studying and performing ancient ceremonies, an astradhari learns how to summon a special version of an enhanced [armor], [shield] or [weapon] veil, or a constellation in either weapon or armor form. Such summoned arms are called astras.

Starting at 1st level, an astradhari adds 1 astra, either an enhanced veil or constellation that has a weapon or armor form, to the list of astras that they can summon with this ability, plus a number of additional astras equal to their Intelligence modifier.

At 3rd level, and every odd level thereafter, they learn to summon an additional astra.

Similar to a wizard learning new spells, an astradhari can learn new summoning ceremonies from other sources. If an astradhari reads or hears a legend detailing an appropriate astra, or watches a character wielding it, they can attempt to trace its connection with the Akashic Records and learn how to summon it. This is done by meditating for an hour and rolling a Knowledge (arcana) check against a base DC that depends on how much detail they are able to gather or observe:

Detailed knowledge (DC 15): Has access to a detailed text on the stories, history, and legends concerning the veil or constellation. Instruction over the course of at least an 8 uninterrupted hours by a character that can shape the veil or manifest the constellation. A description of a veil or constellation provided a character with the summon astra ability.

Casual knowledge (DC 20): Previously observed the veil or constellation closely, usually by making a successful check to fully identify it. A description of the veil or constellation provided by a character that is a veilweaver or starcaller that can either shape or manifest it.

Sparse or second hand knowledge (DC 25+): Seen a veil or constellation, identified it as such, but failed to identify its properties.A description of the veil or constellation provided a character that is not a veilweaver or starcaller, hearing a vague legend from a traveling bard. This DC can be higher based on the vagueness of the information at GM discretion. This DC increases based on the highest tier of chakra it can be bound to as follows: lesser +1, middle +2, esoteric (ring, voice, ect.) +3, high +4, and highest +5; +1 for each additional chakra it can be bound to.

For example, the Knowledge (arcana) DC for the astradhari to learn the ceremony for the Trishula of the Sun enhanced veil would be 27 (20 + 5 for the highest bind [body] + 2 for it having 2 other binds).

If they are attempting to learn a constellation as an astra, the base DC is increased by an amount equal to the base essence burn cost of the constellation form they are trying to learn. The weapon and armor manifestations of a constellation must be learned separately.

If the skill check fails, the astradhari cannot attempt to learn that particular astra again until the next day.

Summoning an astra learned in this way normally requires a full-round action. However, by increasing the DC to learn a veil or constellation as an astra by 10, the astradhari can try to learn how to summon an astra as a standard action. There is no maximum number of astras that the astradhari can learn in this way. Note, some veils and constellation are beyond what an astradhari can learn using this ability (e.g. emblem veils and constellations that are unique to specific class, archetype, or ability [e.g. the Maya constellation gained by a Chakravartin]).

Chosen Astra (Su)

At 1st level, during their communion with the Akashic records, the astradhari can designate a single astra as their “chosen”. They can summon their chosen astra without spending uses of their astra summoning ability.

An astra summoned in this way remains summoned until dismissed. The astradhari can change their chosen astra when they commune with the akashic record as described in their akashic knowledge ability.

At 4th level, once per day when an astradhari summons an astra, they can designate the newly summoned astra as their chosen astra, while the previously chosen astra becomes a standard astra and disappears after 10 minutes. They gain an additional use of this ability at 12th and 20th levels. At 5th level, they can designate two chosen astras with this ability.

Minor Astras

There are myriad lesser tools and implements that are obscured by the shadows that legendary astras cast. At 1st level, the astradhari learns how to call upon these akashic trinkets and curios to aid them. They gain Shape Minor Veils as a bonus feat even if they don’t meet the prerequisites, and they use Intelligence as their veilweaving modifier for the minor veils granted by this feat.

Astra Bind

Starting at 2nd level, astradhari automatically unlock the chakra bind ability or abilities of any enhanced veil astra they summon. At 2nd level, this includes any lesser chakra binds (Hands, Head or Feet) it can be bound to. At 8th level, it includes middle chakras (Headband, Shoulders or Wrists). At 11th level, this ability includes esoteric chakras (Blood, Ring, Voice etc). At 14th level, this includes the higher chakras (belt or neck). Finally, at 20th level, this ability includes the highest chakras (Body or Chest). If the astradhari summons more than one astra, all astras are treated as bound, even to the same chakra. Astra bind is independent of any veilweaving the astradhari has, and as such the astradhari can shape and bind veils as normal.

Astra Enhancement (Su)

At 2nd level, all summoned enhanced veil astras gain a +1 enhancement bonus, which increases by +1 at each even class level, just like weapon and armor constellations.

The normal rules for stacking enhancement bonuses apply. As long as an astra has at least a +1 enhancement bonus, any additional increases can be spent on special abilities up to a total effective enhancement bonus of +10. In the case of shield astras, the astradhari can chose to enhance them as weapons or armor, or divide the bonus between them. Once chosen, the abilities cannot be changed until the astradhari gains another class level.

The summoned astra is treated like a magical item, and as such it can be affected by spells or effects that enhance items of its type. Imbuement gems can be attached to them if they are enhanced descriptor veils, but they fall off when the veil disappears.

Akashic Style (Su)

Astradhari not only learn how to summon the weapons of the gods and heroes of times past, they also learn how to fight like them. At 2nd level, when summoning their chosen astra, they gain temporary access to one feat from the ranger combat style appropriate to the astra summoned based on the astra’s type as follows:

Melee: two-handed, two-weapon, or weapon and shield combat styles.
Ranged: archery, crossbow or thrown combat styles.
Shield: weapon and shield combat styles.
Armor: heavy armor, light armor, medium armor (see below)
Heavy Armor

Armor Focus, Armor Trick, Cushioning Armor, Intimidating Prowess, Power Attack

At 6th level, add Intense Blows and Poised Bearing to the list.

At 10th level, add Imposing Bearing and Knocking Blows to the list.

Light Armor

Armor Focus, Armor Trick, Dodge, Lightning Reflexes, Mobility

At 6th level, add Improved Lightning Reflexes and Spring Attack to the list

At 10th level, add Counter Reflexes and Sprightly Armor to the list

Medium Armor

Armor Focus, Armor Trick, Combat Reflexes, Cushioning Armor, Ironclad Reactions

At 6th level, add Combat Patrol and Poised Bearing to the list

At 10th level, add Imposing Bearing and Greater Ironclad Reactions to the list

Once a feat is chosen for a given astra for the first time, the astradhari always gains the chosen feat when summoning that astra. At 6th level and every 4 levels thereafter, the astradhari gains access to an additional feat from the same list. Like a ranger, an astradhari ignores any prerequisites of these bonus feats, but can only benefit from them when using their chosen astra. An astradhari can use these bonus feats in any kind of armor. These feats cannot be changed until the character gains another astradhari class level. Astradhari can also choose from the expanded Akashic Combat Style feat lists available to rangers with the Huntsman archetype. Astradhari can only benefit from one fighting style at a time, but can change it when they change their chosen astra, either during their daily communion or when changing chosen astra with their class features.

The GM can allow astradhari to choose from any other combat style allowed in the campaign, even divine combat styles.

Akashic Feat (Su)

During certain moments of their adventuring career, the training of the astradhari takes special focus on the akashic side of their abilities. At 3rd level, and again at every four levels thereafter, the astradhari gains a bonus akashic feat that they meet the prerequisites for.

Astradhari & Racial Veils

If an astradhari has this ability from their race and the veil has the enhanced [armor], [shield] or [weapon] descriptor, they learn it as a bonus astra. Astradhari can still shape it normally if they have veilshaping abilities.

Improved Essence Capacity (Ex)

Astradhari become particularly talented at investing essence. At 3rd, 11th and 19th level, the maximum essence capacity of all their essence receptacles increases by 1.

Improve Astra (Su)

At 4th level, and again at every 4 levels thereafter, the astradhari can improve each of their summoned arsenal. This choice is made for each astra individually. Once chosen, each improvement cannot be changed until the character gains another astradhari class level. The astradhari can choose from the following improvements.

Alignment: The astra is treated as having one alignment for the purposes of bypassing damage reduction and gains the appropriate descriptor. This ability can be chosen more than once.
Deadly: This ability can only be applied to weapon astras. It adds a +2 luck bonus to the wielder’s critical hit confirmation rolls. This ability can be chosen multiple times and its benefits stack.
Efficient Essence: This option can only be taken with constellation astras. It reduces the essence burn cost of summoning the constellation it is applied to as an astra by 1 (minimum 0). This improvement can be chosen more than once.
Enhanced
Essence: This option can only be taken with enhanced veil astras. The affected astra is treated as if it was invested with an additional point of essence for all purposes. This ability can exceed the astradhari’s maximum essence capacity, but doesn’t stack with similar abilities and effects (e.g. the akashic catalyst magic item).
Protective: This ability can only be applied to armor and shield astras. It adds a +2 luck bonus to the user’s AC versus critical hits. This ability can be chosen multiple times and its benefits stack.
Special Material: The summoned item is made from a special material based on the astradhari’s level. At 4th level, the item can be treated as if made of alchemical silver, at 8th level as cold iron or mithral, and at 12th level as adamantine. This ability can be chosen up to three times, treating the items as an alloy having the best qualities of the special materials chosen unless they conflict with each other. The GM can add other special materials to this list at their discretion.
Swift: A swift item acts as if it was one category smaller or lighter for ease of use. A one handed weapon is treated as light (and usable with the weapon finesse feat), while a heavy armor is treated as medium and a medium as light. Armors get their ACP reduced by 1, and increase the maximum Dexterity bonus by +1. This does not allow the astradhari to summon an astra in a size category that does not match their own.
Master of All (Su)

At 20th level, the astradhari becomes a peerless master of their astras and their very existence anchors these summoned armaments to reality. The action required to summon astra becomes a free action. If their chosen astra ability applies to a weapon astra they can make an additional attack with it each round as a part of a full attack with a base attack bonus of +0. If it is an armor or shield, any armor check penalty it inflicts becomes 0, no longer inflicts a speed penalty, and the maximum Dexterity bonus to AC it allows becomes equal to their Dexterity modifier. Additionally, a summoned astra cannot be dismissed by an external force, this includes entering areas of dead magic, as long as the astradhari has at least one point of essence invested in them.

Favored Class Bonuses
All Races: +1/5 point of essence.
All Races with Weapon Familiarity: + 1/4 damage with any astras that take the shape of a weapon included in their weapon familiarity racial feature. This damage is always of the astra’s base damage type.
Dwarves: + 1/4 bonus astra that takes the shape of a weapon from the axes or hammers weapon groups.
Elves: + 1/4 bonus astra that takes the shape of a weapon from the bows or light blades weapon groups.
Gnomes: +1/4 astra improvement to one astra. The gnome must choose a different astra each time to benefit from this ability.
Halflings: + 1/4 racial bonus to one saving throw. A saving throw cannot benefit from this ability again until all saving throws have benefited from it the same number of times.
Humans: + 1/6 akashic style bonus feat added to one of your astras.
Orcs: + 1/4 bonus astra that takes the shape of a weapon from the axes or heavy blades weapon groups.
